classified_claims.text: Every serious attempt to understand reality — no matter how technical, how advanced, how rigorously empirical — quietly depends on something so basic that it almost never gets named: coherence.
classified_claims.location: The Argument in One Page

classified_claims.text: Before equations, before experiments, before data, there is already an expectation in place. Whatever explanation we accept must hold together.
classified_claims.location: The Argument in One Page

classified_claims.text: If you have ever rejected a theory because it "doesn't make sense," you have already applied this rule — whether you noticed it or not.
classified_claims.location: The Argument in One Page

classified_claims.text: Coherence binds because it is the precondition for anything to exist, persist, or mean anything at all.
classified_claims.location: The Argument in One Page

classified_claims.text: It is not discovered within systems. It is enforced upon them by reality itself.
classified_claims.location: The Argument in One Page

classified_claims.text: The ground must be necessary, eternal, immaterial, coherent, and morally good — properties derived from the mathematics, not asserted by theology.
classified_claims.location: The Argument in One Page

classified_claims.text: Christianity satisfies every constraint.
classified_claims.location: The Argument in One Page

classified_claims.text: No other worldview tested satisfies all of them.
classified_claims.location: The Argument in One Page

classified_claims.text: The probability of this occurring by coincidence ranges from 1 in a million to 1 in 100 trillion, depending on independence assumptions.
classified_claims.location: The Argument in One Page

classified_claims.text: The proof generates the lock before anyone goes looking for the key. That eliminates curve-fitting.
classified_claims.location: The Critical Method

classified_claims.text: That is prediction and confirmation, not retrofit.
classified_claims.location: The Critical Method

classified_claims.text: The axioms derive from information theory, not from Christianity.
classified_claims.location: The Critical Method

classified_claims.text: If Christianity fails any axiom, the framework rejects it.
classified_claims.location: The Critical Method

classified_claims.text: It gets the same test as every other worldview — and it is the only one that passes.
classified_claims.location: The Critical Method

classified_claims.text: The Approximate Number System (ANS) is present and measurable in preverbal infants.
classified_claims.location: The Empirical Foundation: Structure Before Culture

classified_claims.text: Behavioral and neural studies demonstrate that infants as young as 3–5 months discriminate numerosity — distinguishing 8 dots from 16 dots, for example — even when total area, density, and other low-level visual features are controlled.
classified_claims.location: The Empirical Foundation: Structure Before Culture

classified_claims.text: Their discrimination follows Weber's law, depending on the ratio between quantities rather than absolute difference.
classified_claims.location: The Empirical Foundation: Structure Before Culture

classified_claims.text: This is not pattern recognition. This is numerical structure.
classified_claims.location: The Empirical Foundation: Structure Before Culture

classified_claims.text: The evidence is longitudinal: ANS acuity measured at 6 months predicts standardized math scores at 3.5 years.
classified_claims.location: The Empirical Foundation: Structure Before Culture

classified_claims.text: Twin studies at 5 months show the sensitivity is partially heritable.
classified_claims.location: The Empirical Foundation: Structure Before Culture

classified_claims.text: EEG work reveals that 3–4-month-old infants display distinct neural signatures when hand-opening actions are numerically congruent versus incongruent with dot arrays — linking number representation to action representation before the infant can crawl, let alone count.
classified_claims.location: The Empirical Foundation: Structure Before Culture

classified_claims.text: These results mean that human cognitive systems do not invent number. They encounter and approximate a structure that is already operative.
classified_claims.location: What the ANS Data Actually Means

classified_claims.text: The most natural reading is that mathematical structure is prior to and independent of specific material configurations and developmental epochs — which is precisely what Axioms A1–A7 in Book I formalize.
classified_claims.location: What the ANS Data Actually Means

classified_claims.text: The receiver did not create the signal. The signal was already there.
classified_claims.location: What the ANS Data Actually Means

classified_claims.text: The helper-versus-hinderer experiments (Hamlin et al.) show that 6– and 10-month-old infants preferentially reach for prosocial agents over antisocial ones in simple climbing scenarios.
classified_claims.location: Moral Evaluation Precedes Socialization

classified_claims.text: At 3 and 6 months, infants look significantly longer at helpers than hinderers.
classified_claims.location: Moral Evaluation Precedes Socialization

classified_claims.text: Follow-up studies demonstrate that infants distinguish helpers from hinderers even when a neutral character is present — they are not merely tracking novelty but evaluating moral valence.
classified_claims.location: Moral Evaluation Precedes Socialization

classified_claims.text: By 4–5 years, children not only prefer helpers but call them "nicer," allocate punishment disproportionately to hinderers, and justify those judgments verbally.
classified_claims.location: Moral Evaluation Precedes Socialization

classified_claims.text: With simplified procedures, 3-year-olds show the same patterns.
classified_claims.location: Moral Evaluation Precedes Socialization

classified_claims.text: This is not learned behavior in any straightforward sense. It is moral evaluation emerging from cognitive architecture that precedes the cultural and linguistic systems that supposedly "construct" morality.
classified_claims.location: Moral Evaluation Precedes Socialization

classified_claims.text: The moral signal is not invented by society. It unfolds from structure — which is exactly what Book III formalizes as the visceral response argument and what Axiom A11 derives from information theory.
classified_claims.location: Moral Evaluation Precedes Socialization

classified_claims.text: These two empirical findings — pre-linguistic numeracy and pre-socialized moral evaluation — are not decorative. They are load-bearing.
classified_claims.location: Why This Matters for the Proof

classified_claims.text: They establish empirically what the formal proof establishes logically: that mathematical truth and moral normativity are not human inventions projected onto an indifferent universe, but features of reality that human cognition is tuned to receive.
classified_claims.location: Why This Matters for the Proof

classified_claims.text: A system whose grounding is entirely within finite, spatiotemporal agents is a closed finite system.
classified_claims.location: Why "Mathematics Is Man-Made" Cannot Close the System

classified_claims.text: It inherits every boundary condition established by Gödel, Chaitin, and the Second Law simultaneously — and therefore cannot account for necessity, universality, or cross-domain applicability.
classified_claims.location: Why "Mathematics Is Man-Made" Cannot Close the System

classified_claims.text: "mathematics is man-made" is only internally consistent if we are willing to surrender three features that mathematics actually exhibits — and that our entire scientific apparatus depends on: Necessity, Universality, Cross-domain applicability.
classified_claims.location: Why "Mathematics Is Man-Made" Cannot Close the System

classified_claims.text: Mathematical truths do not depend on who discovers them or when.
classified_claims.location: Why "Mathematics Is Man-Made" Cannot Close the System

classified_claims.text: The Pythagorean theorem was not "less true" before Pythagoras.
classified_claims.location: Why "Mathematics Is Man-Made" Cannot Close the System

classified_claims.text: If math is grounded in finite agents, its truths are contingent on those agents — but we treat them as necessary.
classified_claims.location: Why "Mathematics Is Man-Made" Cannot Close the System

classified_claims.text: Mathematics works the same in every culture, every epoch, every physical context.
classified_claims.location: Why "Mathematics Is Man-Made" Cannot Close the System

classified_claims.text: If it were genuinely a product of specific brains or cultures, there is no non-miraculous reason it should converge across independent civilizations — yet it does, and the developmental evidence shows it converges even before culture can intervene.
classified_claims.location: Why "Mathematics Is Man-Made" Cannot Close the System

classified_claims.text: Mathematics developed for pure abstraction routinely and precisely describes physical reality — Wigner's "unreasonable effectiveness."
classified_claims.location: Why "Mathematics Is Man-Made" Cannot Close the System

classified_claims.text: If mathematics is merely a human language, this is an extraordinary coincidence with no explanation.
classified_claims.location: Why "Mathematics Is Man-Made" Cannot Close the System

classified_claims.text: If mathematics describes a prior structure that both minds and physical systems participate in, applicability is inevitable.
classified_claims.location: Why "Mathematics Is Man-Made" Cannot Close the System

classified_claims.text: Nominalism relies on robust, stable inferential practices and logical norms that themselves behave like the invariants requiring an external ground.
classified_claims.location: Every Anti-Platonist Option Smuggles In What It Denies

classified_claims.text: Fictionalism treats mathematics as a "story," but the unreasonable success of that story in predicting reality reintroduces the external constraint as "applicability."
classified_claims.location: Every Anti-Platonist Option Smuggles In What It Denies

classified_claims.text: Psychologism grounds math in brains, but then cannot explain why different brains in different centuries converge on the same truths.
classified_claims.location: Every Anti-Platonist Option Smuggles In What It Denies

classified_claims.text: Physicalism grounds math in matter, but then cannot explain why math describes possible physical systems that do not and may never exist.
classified_claims.location: Every Anti-Platonist Option Smuggles In What It Denies

classified_claims.text: The Soteriological Limit shows formally that any position treating mathematical truth as wholly grounded in finite agents collapses into either (a) surrendering the features that make mathematics work, or (b) implicitly depending on a non-finite, prior coherence structure.
classified_claims.location: Every Anti-Platonist Option Smuggles In What It Denies

classified_claims.text: Option (a) is self-defeating. Option (b) is the thesis.
classified_claims.location: Every Anti-Platonist Option Smuggles In What It Denies

classified_claims.text: Axiom 11 demonstrates that the non-deceptive nature of mathematical truth — a moral property — must be inherited from its source, thereby deriving morality from information theory and bridging the is-ought gap without any theological premise.
classified_claims.location: Book I — The Lock: Twenty Axioms from Information Theory

classified_claims.text: A mathematical system cannot prove its own consistency from within (Gödel).
classified_claims.location: Book II — The Architecture: Why the Mathematics Moves This Way

classified_claims.text: Information has irreducible physical cost (Landauer).
classified_claims.location: Book II — The Architecture: Why the Mathematics Moves This Way

classified_claims.text: Randomness is mathematically undecidable (Chaitin).
classified_claims.location: Book II — The Architecture: Why the Mathematics Moves This Way

classified_claims.text: These are not philosophical opinions. They are proven theorems with the same certainty as the Pythagorean theorem.
classified_claims.location: Book II — The Architecture: Why the Mathematics Moves This Way

classified_claims.text: Together they require an external ground.
classified_claims.location: Book II — The Architecture: Why the Mathematics Moves This Way

classified_claims.text: The Coherence Asymmetry Theorem: a person who genuinely rejects the framework must simultaneously use logic (which the framework grounds), trust mathematics (which the framework explains), make moral judgments (which the framework derives), and believe their own reasoning is reliable (which the framework underwrites). The denial is structurally self-refuting.
classified_claims.location: Book III — The Cost of Denial: The Person Who Cannot Exist

classified_claims.text: The Visceral Response Argument: even the person who insists morality is subjective still believes, at a gut level, that some things should not be allowed.
classified_claims.location: Book III — The Cost of Denial: The Person Who Cannot Exist

classified_claims.text: For coherence to be maintained over infinite time, the external source of coherence must be inexhaustible.
classified_claims.location: Book III — The Cost of Denial: The Person Who Cannot Exist

classified_claims.text: Only an infinite source qualifies.
classified_claims.location: Book III — The Cost of Denial: The Person Who Cannot Exist

organization_notes: The document presents a hierarchical argument: foundational axioms about coherence (c1-c5) and information theory (c12) lead to derived properties of the ground (c6), which are then tested against worldviews (c7-c9, c13-c14). Empirical evidence (c15-c33) is presented as load-bearing support for the axioms. The anti-Platonist section (c34-c50) closes an escape hatch. Theorems from mathematics and physics (c52-c56) are cited as proof claims. The argument culminates in theological conclusions (c60). Several claims (c9, c51) lack explicit derivation in this document, creating unsupported leaps.
